detail: ICP34.5 is the most disordered (64.9% IDR), followed by US3 (26.6%) and pUL37 (12.9%). ICP34.5 IDRs are enriched in charged residues (FCR>0.3), consistent with polyampholyte behavior enabling conformational flexibility for multi-partner binding.
significance: High disorder in neurovirulence factor provides structural basis for SLiM-mediated interactions

detail: 196 ELM motif classes screened; 626 high-confidence hits identified (164 in targets). Multi-criteria composite scoring (disorder 0.30, conservation 0.20, accessibility 0.20, flexibility 0.15, CNS relevance 0.15) with pre-defined biologically motivated weights.
significance: Comprehensive SLiM catalog with transparent, non-circular scoring

detail: AlphaFold structures unavailable for HSV-1 proteins; sequence-based exposure estimation identified 548 likely exposed and 1496 moderately exposed SLiMs. 42 strongly competing pairs found.
significance: Majority of predicted SLiMs are surface-accessible, supporting functional relevance

detail: Bipartite network with 190 nodes (11 viral, 179 host) and 614 edges. Greedy modularity detected 4 communities (Q=0.2381). ICP34.5 enriched for MAPK cascade (p=0.005); pUL37 for innate immunity (p=0.026).
significance: Target proteins show pathway-specific rather than broad CNS enrichment

detail: 3695 switch candidates identified; 3542 high confidence. Literature-validated switches include ICP34.5-Beclin1 (autophagy), US3-PKA (apoptosis), and pUL37-TRAF6 (innate immunity). Switch categories: signaling_rewiring(1277), immune_evasion(792), other(660), neuronal_hijacking(427), apoptosis_modulation(366).
significance: Validated molecular mimicry mechanisms recoverable from sequence analysis alone

detail: H1 (CNS targeting: p=0.8606), H2 (switch density: p=0.9083), H3 (CNS switches: p=0.0537): all not significant. This indicates neurovirulence specificity arises from qualitative molecular mechanisms (specific partners: Beclin-1, PP1, TRAF6, BAD) rather than quantitative differences in disorder, SLiM density, or pathway breadth.
significance: Important negative result: HSV-1 neurovirulence is mechanism-specific, not dosage-dependent
